event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: Cboe’s 2022-02-18 Form 10-K ties COVID-19 squarely to multiple operational and financial threats that remain live less than two years after the World Health Organization declared the pandemic.  The filing acknowledges both realised effects (e.g., forced remote-work migration, heightened employee turnover, prior suspension of open-outcry trading) and a spectrum of forward-looking possibilities— from supply-chain interruptions and labour shortages to trading-volume swings and litigation over workplace safety.  Although the company does not quantify dollar impacts, it repeatedly warns that further pandemic developments "could have a material adverse effect" on revenues, cash-flows and liquidity.  The disclosures are more than boiler-plate: they enumerate concrete pressure points such as cyber-security exposure from remote access, “great resignation” staffing risks, and potential disruption of technology-equipment vendors.  Given the recency of the pandemic (within the 0-3-year high-severity window) and the breadth of identified impact channels, the overall risk profile is high, albeit mitigated somewhat by the lack of specific lost-revenue figures or probability estimates.  Accordingly, individual snippet scores cluster in the 4-8 range, reflecting significant but largely un-quantified, still-evolving threats that conform to the Time Decay Principle for a recent event.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic and its effects have had significant impacts on economies around the world.

components.reason: Directly references COVID-19 pandemic.
States that impacts have already been ‘significant’, indicating realised macro-level disruption.
Applies to global economies, implying broad exposure that can cascade to company operations.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic but explicit acknowledgement of significant, ongoing macro impact yields a moderate risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: Further impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, operating results and cash flows.

components.reason: Links pandemic directly to the company (‘our business’).
Uses strong wording ‘material adverse effect’.
Specifies multiple financial dimensions (business, condition, results, cash flows).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: High-impact language and explicit connection to core financial metrics justify an elevated score.

evidence_list.snippet: Governments, public institutions, and other organizations around the world have taken, and may take additional or reimpose previous, emergency measures to combat COVID-19’s spread, including vaccination requirements, implementation of travel bans, stay-at-home orders, border closures, and closures of offices, factories, schools, public buildings and businesses.

components.reason: Details specific pandemic-driven government actions.
Highlights possibility of additional or renewed restrictions (forward-looking uncertainty).
Implications are global and multi-sector, broadening exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Lists concrete government responses that can affect operations, but stops short of quantifying company-specific harm.

evidence_list.snippet: These measures may disrupt the supply chain and may interfere with the ability of our employees, vendors, technology equipment suppliers, data and disaster recovery centers, and other service providers to perform their respective responsibilities and obligations relative to the conduct of our business.

components.reason: Cites potential supply-chain disruption—a core pandemic risk.
Identifies multiple critical stakeholder groups whose performance could be impaired.
Directly links disruptions to the conduct of the company’s business.
Uses conditional ‘may’, signalling uncertainty (mitigating).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific operational choke-points elevate risk, tempered slightly by conditional language.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition to uncertain expenses and impacts to our business we may incur due to COVID-19 as part of us providing a safe and healthy work and trading environment, employees working remotely from different locations and in connection with our return to our offices, we may also be subject to claims from employees or customers alleging failure to maintain safe premises and restrictions with respect to protocols relating to COVID-19.

components.reason: Mentions ‘uncertain expenses’ tied to pandemic safety measures.
Highlights remote-work operational complexities.
Introduces legal liability risk from employee/customer claims.
Future-looking ‘may’ softens certainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Addresses cost and litigation exposures, but speculative phrasing keeps score moderate.

evidence_list.snippet: Further, changes in trading behavior, impacts to trading behavior due to market disruptions, additional temporary suspensions of open outcry trading, temporary regulatory measures and other future developments caused by the effects of COVID-19, including a re-occurrence of cases and the emergence of variants, could impact trading volumes and the demand for our products, market data and services, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, operating results and cash flows and could heighten many of the other risks described herein.

components.reason: Enumerates specific business levers (trading behaviour, open-outcry suspension) sensitive to COVID-19.
Predicts direct hit to core revenue drivers (trading volumes, product demand).
Uses ‘material adverse effect’ language across multiple financial dimensions.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct threat to principal revenue streams with severe wording justifies a high score.

evidence_list.snippet: Our increased adoption of remote working, initially driven by the COVID-19 pandemic, usage of mobile and cloud-based technologies and amount of newly acquired companies and related integrations may increase our risk for a cybersecurity incident.

components.reason: Links pandemic-induced remote work to elevated cybersecurity risk.
Identifies specific technological vulnerabilities.
Conditional ‘may’ reduces certainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Narrow operational risk (cyber) tied to pandemic earns a modest score due to conditional tone.

evidence_list.snippet: This competition has become exacerbated by the increase in employee resignations currently taking place throughout the United States as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, which is commonly referred to as the “great resignation,” as well as the growth of new asset classes such as the digital asset space.

components.reason: Explicitly notes workforce attrition linked to COVID-19 (‘great resignation’).
Connects attrition to heightened competitive pressure for talent.
Describes condition as currently occurring (present tense).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Real-time labour-market strain adds moderate operational risk.

evidence_list.snippet: Further, changes in trading behavior, additional suspensions of open outcry trading, market disruptions and other future developments caused by the effects of COVID-19 could impact trading volumes and the demand for our products, market data, and services, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, operating results and cash flows for fiscal year 2021 and could be material during any future period impacted either directly or indirectly by this pandemic.

components.reason: Reiterates risk to trading volumes and product demand from pandemic developments.
Again employs ‘material adverse effect’ language with explicit time horizon.
Specifies potential multi-period materiality (‘any future period’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Confirms sustained, possibly multi-year material exposure, warranting a high score.
